mainTopic: Where does the Torah forbid letting the leftover of a מנחה (the שיריים eaten by the כהנים) become חמץ? A ברייתא uses ״לא תאפה חמץ״ for separate liability for each stage of making the dough, so the גמרא answers that the source is the next word, ״חלקם״.
overview: The גמרא wants a source for the rule that the שיריים of a מנחה, the part the כהנים eat, may not become חמץ. A ברייתא uses ״לא תאפה חמץ״ for a different lesson: each step of making a מנחה into חמץ, such as kneading, shaping, smoothing and baking, gets its own lashes. So the גמרא says the rule about the שיריים comes from the next word, ״חלקם״, and the unusual word order lets the פסוק teach both laws. The גמרא then asks why ״לא תעשה״ and ״לא תאפה״ are not read as a כלל ופרט, which would limit the ban to baking alone. רבי אפטוריקי answers that verses far apart in the תורה are not read as a כלל ופרט. רב אדא בר אהבה challenges this from a ברייתא about where the king's goat חטאת is slaughtered, in the צפון. רב אשי shows that those verses are really a פרט וכלל, so the ברייתא's idea came from the limiting word אֹתוֹ, and the rule stands. Finally, the גמרא explains that אֹתוֹ leaves out the goat of נחשון, which does not need the צפון even though it does need סמיכה. It then begins a ברייתא about the source for that סמיכה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does the Torah repeat the ban on leaven?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the פסוק says ״לא תאפה חמץ״ when ״לא תעשה חמץ״ was already said.
steps.simpleTranslation: "It shall not be baked with leaven": why does the verse need to say this? Hasn't it already said "It shall not be made with leaven"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a ברייתא that asks why the Torah says ״לא תאפה חמץ״ at all. This sets up the ברייתא's own answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah already forbade making a מנחה into חמץ in ויקרא פרק ב. So the second פסוק in ויקרא פרק ו looks extra, and the ברייתא assumes an extra phrase must be teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the verse need to say this? (The phrase looks extra.)
But it was already stated!
Leavened dough. A מנחה may not be made this way.

phrases.english: "[It shall not] be baked with leaven": what does the verse come to teach?
phrases.notes: The word לא ("not") came at the end of the line before. The פסוק is ויקרא 6:10.

phrases.english: But wasn't it already stated:
"It shall not be made with leaven"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:11

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר? וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא brings this ברייתא to test the earlier claim that ״לא תאפה חמץ״ teaches the rule about the שיריים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new rule does ״לא תאפה חמץ״ teach, if ״לא תעשה חמץ״ already forbids leaven in a מנחה?

steps.title: Separate liability for baking
steps.stepSummary: Without the second פסוק, we might think there is only one punishment for the whole process. ״לא תאפה״ teaches that each step is punished separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Torah said "It shall not be made with leaven", you might think a person is liable only once for all the steps. So the verse says "It shall not be baked".
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. ״לא תאפה״ teaches that a person can be punished more than once for making a מנחה into חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״לא תעשה חמץ״ is general. It could mean the whole process of making leavened dough counts as one sin, with only one set of lashes. By naming baking separately, the Torah shows that the steps are counted one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (a mistaken idea that the verse then corrects)
One punishment for all of them together
"It shall not be baked": the extra phrase being explained

phrases.english: Since it says "It shall not be made with leaven,"
one might think he would not be liable
except once for all of them?
phrases.notes: "All of them" means all the steps of making the dough, like kneading, shaping and baking.

phrases.english: So the verse says: "It shall not be baked."

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״לֹא תֵעָשֶׂה חָמֵץ״, יָכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״לא תאפה״ teaches that a person is not punished only once for the whole process; baking carries its own liability.

steps.title: Baking as the model for kneading and shaping
steps.stepSummary: Baking was already included in the general ban. It was singled out to serve as a model, so kneading and shaping are each punished separately too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Baking was already included in the general rule. Why was it mentioned by itself? To compare the other steps to it. Just as baking is a separate action and one is liable for it by itself, so too I will include kneading and shaping.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how ״לא תאפה״ teaches separate liability for every step, not only for baking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Baking was already covered by ״לא תעשה חמץ״. When the Torah pulls one example out of a general rule, it becomes a model for the rest. Baking is one distinct action that is punished on its own, so kneading and shaping, which are also distinct actions, are each punished on their own too.

keyTerms.meaning: It was already included in the general rule
It was singled out to serve as a comparison for the others
A single, distinct action
Kneading and shaping the dough

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think only baking is punished separately. Baking is just the model; every distinct step gets its own liability.

phrases.english: Baking was included in the general rule,
phrases.notes: The general rule is ״לא תעשה חמץ״, which already covered every step, baking included.

phrases.english: why was it singled out? To compare to it:
just as baking is special
in that it is a single action,
and one is liable for it by itself,
so too I will include its kneading and its shaping.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִיָּיה בַּכְּלָל הָיָתָה, לָמָּה יָצָאת לְהַקִּישׁ אֵלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the answer in step 2 reaches beyond baking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kneading and shaping a מנחה into חמץ are each punished separately, learned by comparing them to baking.

steps.title: Even smoothing the dough counts separately
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds "every single action". The גמרא explains this includes smoothing the dough's surface, which is also a separate punishable act.
steps.simpleTranslation: And every single action in it: this comes to include smoothing, which is a single action, and one is liable for it by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא widens the rule to every distinct step of making the dough. The גמרא explains that this phrase comes to include smoothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Smoothing the dough is a small step, but it is still its own action. So it too fits the model of baking and carries separate liability. Now the ברייתא has used ״לא תאפה״ completely for this rule, which leaves the earlier proof about the שיריים without a source.

keyTerms.meaning: To include (this phrase comes to add another case)
Smoothing the surface of the dough with water
By itself, separately

steps.whyThisMatters: Since ״לא תאפה חמץ״ is used up for this rule, the גמרא's earlier proof about the שיריים is now in question, and the next step answers that.

phrases.english: and every single action in it,
this comes to include smoothing,
phrases.notes: Smoothing means wetting the top of the dough to make it smooth.

phrases.english: since it is a single action,
and one is liable for it by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל מַעֲשֶׂה יְחִידִי שֶׁבָּהּ, לְאֵיתוֹיֵי קִיטּוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the comparison in step 3 to every distinct action, including smoothing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Smoothing the dough of a מנחה that is חמץ is also punished separately.

steps.title: The source is the word חלקם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ban on letting the שיריים become חמץ comes from the word ״חלקם״, not from ״לא תאפה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are saying it from "their portion".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the problem raised by the ברייתא. Its proof about the שיריים rests on the next word in the פסוק, ״חלקם״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used ״לא תאפה חמץ״ for separate liability for each step. But the פסוק continues with ״חלקם״, "their portion", which refers to the part the כהנים eat. That word teaches that the כהנים' portion, the שיריים, must also not become חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: "Their portion": the part of the מנחה that the כהנים eat
We are saying (we meant it this way)
The leftover of a מנחה, eaten by the כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: ״לא תאפה חמץ״ teaches separate lashes for each step of making the dough, like kneading, shaping, baking and smoothing. The ban on letting the שיריים become חמץ comes from the word ״חלקם״.

phrases.english: We are saying it from "their portion."
phrases.notes: It's the word right after ״לא תאפה חמץ״ in the same פסוק, ויקרא 6:10.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנַן מֵ״חֶלְקָם״ קָאָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem created by the ברייתא in steps 1 through 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the source to a different word in the same פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on the שיריים seemed to rest on ״לא תאפה חמץ״, which the ברייתא had already used for another rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban on the שיריים comes from ״חלקם״, and ״לא תאפה״ stays free for the ברייתא's rule.

steps.title: Maybe the whole phrase only teaches about the leftovers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if ״חלקם״ teaches the ban on letting the שיריים become חמץ, maybe the whole phrase is there only for that, and nothing teaches separate punishments.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that the whole phrase comes only for this purpose (the leftovers)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer from step 5. If this part of the פסוק is about the leftovers, maybe that is all it teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 the גמרא said the ban on letting the שיריים become חמץ comes from ״חלקם״. Now it worries that the whole phrase ״לא תאפה חמץ חלקם״ might be used up by that one law. Then there would be no source left for punishing each step separately, which was the lesson of steps 2–4.

keyTerms.meaning: But maybe say; the opening of a challenge that offers another reading
The whole thing comes for this purpose only
The leftover part of the מנחה that the כהנים eat

phrases.english: But say: the whole of it comes for this purpose?
phrases.notes: "This purpose" means the ban on letting the leftovers become חמץ, from step 5.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: כּוּלֵּיהּ לְהָכִי הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the answer in step 5 uses up the פסוק and leaves nothing for step 2's teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that ״לא תאפה חמץ״ teaches a separate punishment for each step
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the phrase is needed for the leftovers law, it cannot also be the source for separate punishments.

steps.title: The word order shows the פסוק teaches two things
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק only meant the leftovers, it would say ״חלקם לא תאפה חמץ״. Since it puts ״חלקם״ at the end, it teaches both laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פסוק should have written: "Their portion shall not be baked with leaven." Why does it say: "It shall not be baked with leaven; their portion"? Learn from it two things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by looking at the order of the words in the פסוק. Because of that order, the phrase can teach two separate laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Had the Torah wanted only the leftovers law, it would have put ״חלקם״ first and tied it to the ban. Instead ״לא תאפה חמץ״ stands on its own first, so it teaches the separate punishments. ״חלקם״, which comes after it, teaches the leftovers law.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; introduces what we would expect if the challenger were right
Let the פסוק write (it should have said)
Learn two things from it
Their portion; the כהנים's share of the מנחה

phrases.english: If so, let it write:
"Their portion shall not be baked with leaven,"
why does it say "It shall not be baked with leaven; their portion"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:10

phrases.english: Learn from it two things.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לִכְתּוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading from word order: the unusual order shows two teachings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase only teaches about the leftovers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase teaches both separate punishments and the leftovers ban.
steps.whatToRemember: ״לא תאפה חמץ״ teaches separate punishments; ״חלקם״ teaches the leftovers ban. The word order lets one phrase carry both.

steps.title: Maybe only baking gets its own punishment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that baking, which the Torah names, gets one punishment, while all the other steps together get just one more.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: baking, which the Merciful One spelled out, brings one punishment; the other steps together bring one punishment for all of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a smaller reading of the פסוק. Baking is named, so it stands alone, but the unnamed steps might share one punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 said baking was singled out as a model for all the steps. This challenge says the singling out might only make baking itself separate. Kneading, shaping and smoothing would then be lumped together under the general ban of ״לא תעשה״, with one punishment between them.

keyTerms.meaning: Baking
The Merciful One (the Torah) spelled it out by name
Let him be liable for one (one set of lashes)
Those others; the remaining steps

phrases.english: But say: baking,
which the Merciful One spelled out,
let him be liable for one;
phrases.notes: "One" here means one set of lashes.

phrases.english: the others, let him be liable for one for all of them!
phrases.notes: "The others" are kneading, shaping and smoothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: אֲפִיָּיה, דִּפְרַט בַּהּ רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the source is secure, the גמרא challenges how far the lesson reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 3's claim that baking is a model for every other step
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Naming baking could make only baking separate, leaving the other steps grouped together.

steps.title: Baking was singled out to teach about every step
steps.stepSummary: Baking was part of the general ban and was named to teach a lesson. A case like that teaches about the whole group, not only about itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is something that was included in the general rule and came out of the general rule to teach. It did not come out to teach about itself alone; it came out to teach about the whole general rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a well-known rule for reading the Torah. When one case is pulled out of a group to teach something, the lesson applies to the whole group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Baking was already forbidden under ״לא תעשה״. The Torah names it again, and that extra mention is a lesson for the whole group: each step is its own sin. So kneading, shaping and smoothing each get their own punishment, just like baking.

keyTerms.term: דָּבָר שֶׁהָיָה בַּכְּלָל וְיָצָא מִן הַכְּלָל לְלַמֵּד
keyTerms.meaning: Something included in a general rule that was singled out to teach a lesson
A general rule or statement
About itself alone

phrases.english: Because it is something

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה בַּכְּלָל וְיָצָא מִן הַכְּלָל לְלַמֵּד,
phrases.english: that was included in the general rule and came out of the general rule to teach,
phrases.notes: The general rule is ״לא תעשה חמץ״, which already covered baking.

phrases.english: it did not come out to teach about itself,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְלַמֵּד עַל הַכְּלָל כּוּלּוֹ יָצָא.
phrases.english: rather it came out to teach about the whole general rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה דָּבָר שֶׁהָיָה בַּכְּלָל וְיָצָא מִן הַכְּלָל לְלַמֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by naming the rule behind step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying a standard rule for reading the Torah
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only baking is separate; the other steps share one punishment.
steps.terutzMaskana: Every step, like baking, brings its own punishment.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think baking is the only step punished separately. The point is the opposite: naming baking teaches that every step is separate.

steps.title: Maybe a general rule followed by a detail limits the ban to baking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a different rule, כלל ופרט. By that rule, ״לא תעשה״ is the general statement and ״לא תאפה״ is the detail, so only baking would be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: "shall not be made" is a general statement and "shall not be baked" is a detail. With a general statement followed by a detail, the general statement includes only what is in the detail. Baking, yes; other things, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new and stronger challenge from another rule for reading the Torah. This would shrink the whole ban down to baking alone. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rule of כלל ופרט, a broad word followed by a specific example is limited to that example. That would mean kneading and shaping are not forbidden at all with חמץ, not just that they share a punishment. This attack is bigger than the one in step 8, because it threatens the ban itself.

keyTerms.meaning: A general statement followed by a detail; the general covers only the detail
A detail or specific example
Yes
Other things

phrases.english: But say: "shall not be made" is a general statement,
"shall not be baked" is a detail,

phrases.aramaic: כְּלָל וּפְרָט – אֵין בַּכְּלָל אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁבַּפְּרָט;
phrases.english: general and detail: the general includes only what is in the detail;
baking, yes; other things, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: ״לֹא תֵעָשֶׂה״ – כָּלַל, ״לֹא תֵאָפֶה״ – פָּרַט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 9 by reading the same two פסוקים with a different rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 9's use of דבר שהיה בכלל ויצא, and the ban on the other steps
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two phrases are a כלל ופרט, the ban covers only baking, and the other steps are not forbidden at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: The two rules give opposite results: one widens the lesson to every step, the other narrows it to baking. The גמרא must explain why כלל ופרט does not apply here.

steps.title: Verses far apart are not read as a general statement and a detail
steps.stepSummary: רבי אפטוריקי says the rule of כלל ופרט does not apply here, because the two verses are far apart in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אפטוריקי said: This is a general statement and a detail that are far from each other. Any general statement and detail that are far from each other are not judged by the rule of general and detail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 10. The rule of כלל ופרט does not apply here, because ״לא תעשה״ and ״לא תאפה״ are far apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 tried to say that only baking is forbidden, since a כלל followed by a פרט covers only the פרט. רבי אפטוריקי limits that rule. It works only when the general and the detail are close together, and here they are in different chapters. So all the steps of making חמץ are still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A general statement followed by a detail. The rule is that only the detail is included.
Far apart from each other in the Torah
We do not judge or learn by this method

phrases.english: Rabbi Aptoriki said:
Because it is a general statement and a detail
phrases.notes: ״לא תעשה״ is in ויקרא 2:11, and ״לא תאפה״ is in ויקרא 6:10, chapters away from each other.

phrases.english: that are far from each other,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל כְּלָל וּפְרָט הַמְרוּחָקִין זֶה מִזֶּה –
phrases.english: and any general statement and detail that are far from each other
we do not judge them by the rule of general and detail.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי אפטוריקי משום דהוי כלל ופרט המרוחקין זה מזה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the כלל ופרט challenge of Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of a rule for learning from verses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every כלל followed by a פרט limits the law to the פרט, so only baking would be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: כלל ופרט applies only when the two verses are near each other. Here they are far apart, so every step of making חמץ stays forbidden.

steps.title: A challenge from a teaching about the king's goat offering
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה questions רבי אפטוריקי's rule. He quotes a ברייתא that learns from verses about where a חטאת is slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה objected, and some say the question is quoted without a name: Is it true that we do not judge far-apart verses as a general statement and detail? But a ברייתא teaches: "And he shall slaughter it in the place where they slaughter the burnt offering before ה׳; it is a sin offering." Where is the burnt offering slaughtered? In the north. So this one too is slaughtered in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אפטוריקי's rule and begins quoting a ברייתא. This step is setup, since the full force of the challenge comes after the ברייתא is fully quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about the שעיר נשיא, the goat a king brings as a חטאת. It learns from the עולה that this goat must be slaughtered in the צפון. The ברייתא goes on to compare verses about חטאת that are spread far apart in the Torah. That is why רב אדא sees it as a problem for the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Without a name, said by no named person
A burnt offering
A sin offering
The north side of the Temple courtyard

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava objects,
and some say it was asked without a name:
And a general statement and a detail that are far from each other
we do not judge them by the rule of general and detail?
But isn't it taught:
"And he shall slaughter it in the place where they slaughter the burnt offering
before ה׳; it is a sin offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:24. This פסוק is about the goat a king brings.

phrases.english: Where is the burnt offering slaughtered? In the north,
so this one too is in the north.

steps.triggerLanguage: מתיב רב אדא בר אהבה ואמרי לה כדי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule just stated in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אפטוריקי's rule that far-apart verses are not read as כלל ופרט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא learns from verses about חטאת that are spread far apart in the Torah. This seems to show that far-apart verses can be read together.

steps.title: Why does the Torah repeat this law
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the king's goat needs its own verse, since another verse already says every חטאת is slaughtered where the עולה is.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do we learn it from here? Wasn't it already stated: "In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the sin offering shall be slaughtered"? So why was this one singled out?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question about itself. If another verse already teaches that a חטאת goes in the צפון, why does the king's goat need its own verse?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in ויקרא 6:18 already gives the general law for all חטאות. That makes the verse about the king's goat look extra. The ברייתא now looks for a new lesson that this extra verse teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we really learn this law from here?
So why was this one singled out?

steps.title: The extra verse makes the north a must
steps.stepSummary: The extra verse teaches that the צפון is required, so a חטאת slaughtered anywhere else is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: To make it fixed: if he did not slaughter it in the north, he made it invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The extra verse teaches that slaughtering in the צפון is required, not just the proper way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the extra verse, the צפון might be only the right way to do it from the start (לכתחילה). The repeated verse fixes the צפון as a must, so even after the fact (בדיעבד) a חטאת slaughtered elsewhere is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: To make it fixed and required
He made it invalid
After the fact, once it was already done

phrases.english: To make it fixed,

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The repeated verse teaches that the צפון is required, and a חטאת slaughtered elsewhere is פסול.

steps.title: Maybe only this goat needs the north
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests another reading: maybe the verse means that only the king's goat needs the צפון and no other goat does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it came out for this? Or perhaps it only means that this one needs the north and no other needs the north?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tests its own answer by offering another way to read the verse. Maybe the verse limits the צפון to the king's goat alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the verse only teaches that the king's goat needs the צפון, then other goat חטאות would not need it. If that were true, the verse could not be used to teach that the צפון is a must.

keyTerms.meaning: Requires or needs
Do you say it came out for this purpose?

phrases.english: Do you say it came out for this,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא שֶׁזֶּה טָעוּן צָפוֹן

steps.triggerLanguage: אתה אומר לכך יצאת או אינו אלא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the answer given in Step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the verse teach that the צפון is a must, or that only the king's goat needs the צפון?

steps.title: Another verse teaches the north for all sin offerings
steps.stepSummary: Another verse already sets up a בנין אב that all חטאות need the צפון. So the king's verse is free to teach that the צפון is a must.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "And he shall slaughter the sin offering in the place where he slaughters the burnt offering." This set up a model for all sin offerings, that they need the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers by pointing to another verse that already teaches the צפון for every חטאת. So the king's verse is not needed to teach that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ויקרא 4:29 builds a בנין אב, a model case, for all חטאות. So the king's verse cannot mean that only his goat needs the צפון. Its lesson must be the one from Step 14: the צפון is a must.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches
Set up a model case that teaches about a whole group

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא learns about every חטאת by putting together verses from different places in the Torah. The גמרא will use this to challenge רבי אפטוריקי's rule that far-apart verses are not read together.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And he shall slaughter the sin offering
in the place where he slaughters the burnt offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:29. This verse is about an ordinary person's חטאת.

phrases.english: This set up a model for all sin offerings
that they need the north.

steps.triggerLanguage: תלמוד לומר ושחט את החטאת במקום אשר ישחט את העולה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15 and confirms the answer of Step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 4:29 is a בנין אב that all חטאות need the צפון. So the king's verse teaches that the צפון is a must.

steps.title: Why would we have limited the צפון to the king's goat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא looks closely at the ברייתא. It sees that, without the extra verse, the ברייתא would have said only the king's goat needs the צפון, and asks what the reason for that idea is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא needed the verse 'and he shall slaughter the חטאת in the place of the עולה.' That means that without it, we would have said only this one (the king's goat) needs the צפון and no other does. What is the reason we would have thought that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks where the ברייתא's first idea, that only the king's goat needs the צפון, came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is already a verse that seems to cover every חטאת, so it is strange that the ברייתא could think only the king's goat needs the צפון. The גמרא wants to find the source of that mistaken idea, because the answer will decide whether רבי אפטוריקי's rule is in trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, a name for ה׳ as the author of the תורה
I would have said; the first idea before the conclusion
Must be slaughtered in the north side of the courtyard
What is the reason?

phrases.english: The reason is that the Merciful One wrote
"And he shall slaughter the sin offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:29

phrases.english: which means that if not for this
I would have said that this one requires the north
and no other requires the north.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads into the ברייתא from steps 15-16 and asks about the source of its first idea.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did the ברייתא first think that only the king's goat needs the צפון?

steps.title: It must be a כלל ופרט even though the verses are far apart
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the reason is a כלל ופרט built from two distant verses. That would show that distant verses can make a כלל ופרט, which goes against רבי אפטוריקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it because it is a general statement followed by a detail? And even though they are far from each other, we still judge them by the rule of כלל ופרט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The idea must have come from a כלל ופרט, and that finishes רב אדא בר אהבה's challenge to רבי אפטוריקי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a כלל ופרט, the detail limits the general statement, so only the detail is included. If the general verse about all חטאות is limited by the king's verse, we get 'only the king's goat.' But these verses are far apart, so the ברייתא would be using a distant כלל ופרט, which רבי אפטוריקי said we do not do.

keyTerms.meaning: A general statement followed by a detail; only what the detail names is included
Far apart from each other in the תורה
We derive / we judge (by a rule of learning verses)

phrases.english: Isn't it because it is a general statement and a detail,
phrases.notes: The general part is the verse about every חטאת; the detail is the verse about the king's goat.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דִּמְרוּחָקִין זֶה מִזֶּה,
phrases.english: and even though they are far from each other,
we judge them by the rule of general and detail.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה כְּלָל וּפְרָט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17's question in a way that completes the challenge from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אפטוריקי's rule that verses far apart are not read as a כלל ופרט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's first idea only makes sense as a כלל ופרט made of two distant verses, so the ברייתא treats distant verses as a כלל ופרט.

steps.title: רב אשי: it is really a פרט וכלל, which includes everything
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי pushes back. The king's verse comes first in the תורה, so the order is detail, then general. In a פרט וכלל the general part adds to the detail and includes everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: Is this a general followed by a detail?! It is a detail followed by a general! Then the general adds to the detail, and everything is included.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects the idea that the ברייתא was using a כלל ופרט. The order of the verses makes it a פרט וכלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king's goat verse (ויקרא 4) comes before the verse about all חטאות (ויקרא 6). In a פרט וכלל, the later general statement widens things to include every case. So this reading would never produce 'only the king's goat,' and it cannot be the source of the ברייתא's first idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenges / objects strongly
A detail followed by a general statement
The general statement adds to the detail, so more cases are included
They are included

steps.confusionAlert: Order matters. In a כלל ופרט, general then detail, only the detail is included. In a פרט וכלל, detail then general, everything is included. They come out opposite.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objected to it:
Is this a general and a detail?!
It is a detail and a general,
phrases.notes: The king's verse (ויקרא 4:24) comes earlier than the verse about all חטאות (ויקרא 6:18).

phrases.english: and the general becomes an addition to the detail,
and all things are included.
phrases.notes: Some versions say the round-bracket word; the square-bracket word is the corrected wording. Both mean 'included.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 18's claim that the verses form a כלל ופרט.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the ברייתא's first thought came from a distant כלל ופרט
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verses are in the order detail then general, and that order includes everything instead of limiting.

steps.title: The real source: the word אֹתוֹ ("it") in the king's verse
steps.stepSummary: Instead, the ברייתא's first idea came from the word אֹתוֹ in the king's verse. That word sounds like a limit: 'this one only.' So the ברייתא is no proof against רבי אפטוריקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the word 'it' was difficult for the תנא. This is what he means: Or perhaps only this one needs the north and no other does, since the Merciful One wrote 'it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of the ברייתא. Its first idea came from the word אֹתוֹ, not from a כלל ופרט, so רבי אפטוריקי's rule stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king's verse says 'and he shall slaughter it,' and 'it' can be read as 'only it.' That limiting word, not a distant כלל ופרט, made the תנא think only the king's goat needs the צפון. Since no distant כלל ופרט is involved, the challenge to רבי אפטוריקי falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; brings in a new explanation
The teacher of the ברייתא
'It'; here read as a limiting word: 'only it'
It was difficult for him

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's thought 'only the king's goat needs the צפון' comes from the limiting word אֹתוֹ, not from a כלל ופרט. So the ברייתא does not disprove רבי אפטוריקי's rule that verses far apart are not read as a כלל ופרט.
steps.whyThisMatters: It saves רבי אפטוריקי's rule and shows that, before treating verses as a כלל ופרט, we must check their order and look for other limiting words.

phrases.english: Rather, the תנא,
the word "it" was difficult for him,
phrases.notes: From the king's פסוק, 'and he shall slaughter it' (ויקרא 4:24). 'It' sounds like 'only it.'

phrases.english: and this is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא שֶׁזֶּה טָעוּן צָפוֹן
phrases.english: Or perhaps it is only that this one requires the north
and no other requires the north,
since the Merciful One wrote "it."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תַּנָּא, ״אֹתוֹ״ קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 19 rejects the כלל ופרט reading, this gives the real reason for the ברייתא's first idea.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source of the ברייתא's first idea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's first idea came from a distant כלל ופרט, which would go against רבי אפטוריקי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first idea came from the limiting word אֹתוֹ, so the ברייתא says nothing about distant verses and רבי אפטוריקי's rule stands.

steps.title: What does the word 'it' leave out now?
steps.stepSummary: The צפון rule comes from 'וְשָׁחַט אֶת הַחַטָּאת'. So what is אֹתוֹ there to leave out?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that the rule is learned from 'and he shall slaughter the sin offering,' what does the word 'it' come to leave out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. If אֹתוֹ is not what teaches the צפון rule, what is it doing in the פסוק?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 the גמרא said the ברייתא's first idea came from אֹתוֹ. But the final rule that all חטאות need the צפון comes from another verse. So אֹתוֹ is now free, and every word in the תורה must teach something. The גמרא asks what it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: And now, meaning: now that we have reached this conclusion
To leave out, to exclude
'It'. A word that sounds like a limit: only this one

phrases.english: And now that he derives it
from 'and he shall slaughter the sin offering,'

phrases.english: what does 'it' come to exclude?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּנָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״וְשָׁחַט אֶת הַחַטָּאת״, ״אֹתוֹ״ לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 20. Now that the צפון rule comes from another verse, the word אֹתוֹ needs a new job.

steps.title: The word 'it' leaves out the goat of נחשון
steps.stepSummary: After listing a memory aid for what is coming, the גמרא answers: אֹתוֹ needs the צפון, but נחשון's goat does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: To leave out (memory aid: נחשון, ושחט, עוף, בפסח). 'It' is slaughtered in the north, but the goat of נחשון is not slaughtered in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אֹתוֹ leaves out the goat that נחשון brought. That goat did not have to be slaughtered in the צפון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אֹתוֹ means 'this kind of חטאת', and not every goat called a חטאת. נחשון's goat is called a חטאת in the תורה, yet it does not get the צפון rule. The memory aid lists the topics the גמרא will go through next.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid: a short list of key words to help remember the coming topics
The goat brought as a חטאת by נחשון, the נשיא of שבט יהודה, at the dedication of the משכן

phrases.english: To exclude (mnemonic: Nahshon, and slaughter, bird, on Passover).

phrases.english: 'It' is in the north,
but the goat of Nahshon is not in the north.
phrases.notes: See במדבר 7. Each נשיא brought offerings when the משכן was dedicated.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אֹתוֹ leaves out שעיר נחשון, which did not need slaughter in the צפון.
steps.confusionAlert: The word סימן at the start is not part of the answer. It is only a memory list. The real answer is the line about נחשון's goat.

steps.title: Why we needed a verse to leave out נחשון's goat
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought that נחשון's goat needs the צפון because it needs סמיכה. So the verse teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since it is included in the rule of סמיכה, let it also be included in the rule of the north. So the verse teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the verse had to leave out נחשון's goat. Without אֹתוֹ, someone could have made a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחשון's goat already shares one rule with a regular חטאת: placing hands on it (סמיכה). So we might have thought it shares the צפון rule too. אֹתוֹ stops that thought: the sharing goes only as far as סמיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: It could enter your mind to say. This introduces a mistaken idea that the תורה has to block
It was included in a rule
Leaning one's hands on the head of a קרבן before it is slaughtered
It comes to teach us

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:
since it is included regarding placing hands,

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since נחשון's goat needs סמיכה, we might have thought it also needs the צפון. אֹתוֹ prevents that mistake.

steps.title: Where do we learn that נחשון's goat needs סמיכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the claim that נחשון's goat needed סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rule of סמיכה itself, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 23 assumed that נחשון's goat needed סמיכה. Now the גמרא stops to ask how we know that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole reason for the mistaken idea in step 23 rests on סמיכה applying to נחשון's goat. So the גמרא wants a source for that starting point before going on.

keyTerms.meaning: Itself. Here it means the point that was just assumed
From where do we know it? A request for a source

phrases.english: And placing hands itself, from where do we derive it?
phrases.notes: He means: how do we know נחשון's goat needed סמיכה at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּסְמִיכָה גּוּפַהּ מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the assumption made in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that שעיר נחשון required סמיכה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns it from 'the head of the goat'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that the words 'the head of the goat' include נחשון's goat in סמיכה, according to רבי יהודה. Then רבי שמעון begins to give a different view.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'And he shall place his hand on the head of the goat.' This includes the goat of נחשון in סמיכה. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. רבי יהודה reads the words 'the head of the goat' as including נחשון's goat in the rule of סמיכה. רבי שמעון's opinion starts at the end of this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is the king's own חטאת verse. רבי יהודה says the words 'of the goat' reach out to include another goat called a חטאת, the goat of נחשון. רבי שמעון is about to say something different, and his words continue in the next part.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall place his hand. The verse that commands סמיכה
To include, to add another case to the rule

'And he shall place his hand upon the head of the goat'

phrases.english: to include the goat of Nahshon in placing hands,
the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Shimon says:

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: ״וְסָמַךְ יָדוֹ עַל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׂעִיר״ – לְרַבּוֹת שְׂעִיר נַחְשׁוֹן לִסְמִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי יהודה, 'the head of the goat' (ויקרא 4:24) includes שעיר נחשון in סמיכה.
steps.whatToRemember: נחשון's goat shares סמיכה with a regular חטאת. רבי יהודה learns this from 'the head of the goat.' But because of אֹתוֹ, it does not share the צפון rule.
